tooltips.purpose: Using the RuleMiner application, you can induce three types of rules: decision (classification), regression, and survival patterns. These rules represent patterns - dependencies - that characterize the data and create a predictive system to predict the values of the decision variable. The user should choose the type of analysis they want to perform.
tooltips.classification: Classification: In the context of the RuleMiner system's functionality, it is the process of discovering rules whose premises (specific values of conditional attributes) are associated with specific categorical (symbolic) values of the decision variable. These values should be assigned to examples that meet the conditions specified in the rule premises covering them
tooltips.regression: Regression: In the context of the RuleMiner system's functionality, regression is the process of discovering rules whose premises (specific values of conditional attributes) are associated with specific numerical (quantitative) values of the decision variable. These values should be assigned to examples that meet the conditions specified in the rule premises covering them
tooltips.survival: Survival: In the context of the RuleMiner system's functionality, it is the process of discovering rules whose premises (specific values of conditional attributes) are associated with specific estimators (survival curves; Kaplan-Meier estimators) that determine the probability of "survival" over time for examples that meet the rule premises of the rules
tooltips.separator: Column separator – a character that separates field values in a CSV file. The default value is a comma.
tooltips.decimal: Decimal Separator, Decimal Point: A character used to separate the integer part from the fractional part of a number. The most common separators are a comma or a period
tooltips.missing_values: Missing value indicator: A character used to denote a missing value. In some datasets, missing values are indicated, for example, by the "?" character. In such cases, a question mark should be placed in the field. If the user does not fill in this field, any empty field in individual rows will be considered a missing value
tooltips.column_type: Each column must have its type specified. Columns containing numbers should be designated as numeric, while other columns should be designated as nominal. If columns contain numbers such as 1, 2, 3, which are category names rather than actual numbers, the column should be defined as nominal. The type of each column is determined based on the analysis of the first 10 rows. However, this assignment should be carefully verified. Once the application is in use, it will not be possible to change the column type.
tooltips.classification_tooltip: Decision Attribute.  The decision column must be of nominal.
tooltips.regression_tooltip: Decision Attribute (dependent variable values). The decision column must be of numeric type.
tooltips.survival_time_tooltip: Survival time – a column containing information about the survival time. This column should contain numbers (not dates) and be set as a numeric type.
tooltips.survival_status_tooltip: Survival Status: A column containing information about the occurrence of an event (e.g., death, machine failure). The column must be of nominal type and contain two values: 1 (event occurred) or 0 (no event).

tooltips.scoring: The metric whose value optimized during the hyperparameter space search
tooltips.use_low_correlation_attr_removal: Remove attributes for which the correlation value with the decision attribute is in the range [-0.2, 0.2]. Supported are numerical and binary attributes, where binary attribute values are encoded as numerical values 0 and 1.
tooltips.unimportant_attribute_elimination: Remove attributes for which the values of specified criteria exceed the given thresholds
tooltips.I: Remove nominal attributes with too many unique values
tooltips.S: The value of the indicator is calculated as: the number of rows with the most frequently occurring non-missing value divided by the number of rows with non-missing values
tooltips.M: The value of the indicator is calculated as: the number of missing values for the considered attribute divided by the number of rows
tooltips.T: Remove nominal attributes whose values resemble text - in calculations, considers the number of word separators and the length of the text
tooltips.missing_values_imputation: Fills missing data with a specified value. If not selected, rows with missing values will be dropped.
tooltips.decision_class_balancing: The method uses the SMOTE algorithm to balance the sizes of classes. After applying SMOTE, all classes will have the same number of examples as the originally largest class
tooltips.min_covered_examples: Rules must cover at least - specified parameter value - number of positive examples
tooltips.max_rule_length: Maximum number of elementary conditions that can be included in the premise of a rule
tooltips.beam_width: During the rule growing phase, the beam search strategy is applied. The algorithm analyzes as many temporary solutions as the value of this parameter
tooltips.exclude_target_column: If this option is selected, the decision attribute is not taken into account in the analysis. Otherwise, the decision attribute is treated like any other attribute
tooltips.min_supp: Minimum required support for a frequent set. The value is calculated as the number of occurrences of the frequent set divided by the total number of examples
tooltips.max_rows: Maximum number of best itemsets and association rules to be included in the final result tables
tooltips.min_confidence: Minimum required confidence for association rules
tooltips.max_k_value: Maximum number of attributes forming a frequent set - number of elements forming a frequent set
tooltips.max_intervals_value: Numeric attributes require discretization before determining frequent sets. The report is based on the equal-length interval discretization algorithm

tooltips.treeview: For the selected dataset or ruleset, the user can invoke the context menu

generate_rule.RuleKit: After selecting this option, the rules will be generated automatically. The user only needs to answer a few questions (fill out a form) that will allow for the customization of the induction parameters to suit their needs.
generate_rule.Manually: After selecting this option, the user can define the ruleset manually. They can do this by creating individual rules using the editor or by loading (selecting) rules from existing rulesets. The condition for loading a ruleset is that the rules must match the dataset, meaning they are built based on the conditional attributes present in the dataset.
generate_rule.Manualnie: After selecting this option, the user can define the ruleset manually. They can do this by creating individual rules using the editor or by loading (selecting) rules from existing rulesets. The condition for loading a ruleset is that the rules must match the dataset, meaning they are built based on the conditional attributes present in the dataset.
generate_rule.steeper_generator: Based on the answers provided in the form, the system will automatically set the vules of rule induction parameters. Please remember to accept the submitted answers.
generate_rule.induction: This section allows the user to provide specific requirements for the rule induction algorithm regarding the form of the generated rules.
generate_rule.attributes_to_omit: Specifying attributes (columns) that will not be considered during rule generation.
generate_rule.k_fold: The results of the quality of the rule-based classifier trained in cross-validation mode are available on the "Prediction summary" tab.
generate_rule.DeepRules: A slower rule induction algorithm capable of learning more complex rule sets containing nested logical conjunctions and disjunctions.

rules_table.prediction_from_computer: Allows for making predictions on a dataset that does not contain the decision column. It is important that the submitted dataset has the same conditional attributes (column names) as the dataset for which the ruleset was generated. After clicking the button, the dataset will be uploaded to the server where the prediction will be made using the rule-based model the user is working on. The dataset will then be downloaded with an additional column containing the prediction. The dataset will not be saved in the system. If the user wants to analyze it, they can upload the downloaded dataset to the system.
rules_table.rules_comparison: This tab allows for the examination of rule similarity. Semantic similarity refers to the sets of examples covered by the compared rules. Syntactic similarity refers to the structure of the rules, particularly to the sets of elementary conditions that make up the compared rules.
rules_table.rule_coverage: The tab contains information about the coverage of examples by individual rules. The table below lists the rules along with basic information about each one, such as the premise and conclusion of the rule, as well as the precision and coverage values. Each rule is assigned a color to better illustrate which examples are covered by the given rule. Using the "Show column selection" button, the user can display additional columns. The "Active" marker allows the user to exclude/include a specific rule from/to the analysis.
rules_table.rules: The tab presents a summary of the rules that were generated or obtained by other means. The user has the ability to sort the rules by one or more criteria (columns) by using the keys Shift + header of the "first" column + header of the next column. To disable sorting, click on the header of any column.
rules_table.activity: The "Active" column allows the user to exclude/include a specific rule from/to the ruleset. If a rule is excluded, it is not considered during prediction or when recalculating the values of the metrics characterizing the ruleset.
rules_table.prediction: The values presented in this form provide information about the prediction quality of the active (current) ruleset. Depending on the selected analysis (classification, regression, survival), the form displays the values of the metrics appropriate for the given type of analysis. Detailed information about the metrics and their interpretation can be found in the documentation or on the website https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html.
rules_table.quantitative_characteristics: The values presented in this form provide information about the quality of the rules. Detailed information about the significance of each metric can be found in the documentation.
rules_table.importance: The importance of conditions (attribute importance) reflects the significance of conditions (attributes) for the analyzed ruleset, particularly the rules containing a given condition (attribute). The result of the importance analysis is a ranking of conditions (attributes). The lower the rank of a condition (attribute), the more important it is for the considered rules. In the case of classification, importance is determined separately for each class.
rules_table.filter_rules: The "Filter" function allows the user to filter the dataset by selecting examples that meet the conditions (premises) of the enabled rules. The results of this filtration are visible in the "Data Overview" table (a maximum of {{maxRules}} rules can be selected).
rules_table.visible_coverage: The "Visible coverage" function allows the user to obtain information about which examples are covered by the rules selected by the user. For each of the selected rules (a maximum of {{maxRules}} rules can be selected), a column with the rule's name is added to the "Data Overview" table. The rows in this column indicate which examples are covered by this rule.
rules_table.data_overview: The "Data Overview" table contains information about the values of the conditional attributes for each example. Additionally, the true value (ground truth) of the decision attribute and the prediction made by the ruleset are visible. The table also shows the number of rules covering each example.
rules_table.rules_comapre: This tab allows for the comparison of rule similarity. Two methods are available for analyzing similarity: syntactic and semantic.
rules_table.relation_type: The "one-to-many" comparison type allows comparing one selected rule with many other rules. The "many-to-many" mode enables the examination of the similarity between two sets of rules. Comparisons can be made within a single rule set or between two different rule sets.
rules_table.chosen_metric: This option allows the user to select the metric used to calculate semantic similarity. Detailed formulas for the metrics and the differences between them are described in the documentation.
rules_table.rule_choose_button: The button allows the selection of rulesets for comparison.
rules_table.execute_prediction: In this tab, it is possible to make predictions using the selected ruleset. In the "Data Overview" section, the generated predictions and the true values (if they exist) of the decision attribute for each example are visible.
rules_table.select_dataset_to_execute_prediction: From the dropdown list, select the dataset on which you want to make predictions. For this dataset, the rule-based model will return the predicted values of the decision attribute. Of course, this dataset can be any set, but it must be built with the same attributes as the set used to determine the rules.
rules_table.training_data_set: This section of the form presents statistics describing the quality of predictions on the training set. Details about the metrics used and their interpretation can be found in the documentation or on the website https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html.
rules_table.actual_condition: The confusion matrix provides details on the number of correct and incorrect decisions (including types of errors) made by the rule-based model.
rules_table.specific_decision_class_classification: This section of the form presents classification quality statistics for each decision class separately. The confusion matrices are built on a "class" vs. "all other classes" basis. Details about the quality metrics used and their interpretation can be found in the documentation or on the website https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html.
rules_table.specific_decision_class_regression: This section of the form presents statistics describing the quality of predictions on the training set. Details about the metrics used and their interpretation can be found in the documentation or on the website https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html.
rules_table.similarity_type: Syntactic similarity examines how similar the rules are in terms of their structure, including whether the premises of the rules are built from the same attributes and the range of values of the elementary conditions. Semantic similarity takes into account the sets of examples covered by the compared rules.
rules_table.test_data_set: This section of the form presents statistics describing the quality of predictions on the selected dataset (e.g., test set). Details about the metrics used and their interpretation can be found in the documentation or on the website https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html.
rules_table.cross_validation_results: This section of the form presents statistics on the quality of predictions obtained during cross-validation. The metric values displayed are the average results for the rule-based models generated during the cross-validation process.

create_project.title: Create New Project
create_project.content: Create a new project by clicking here.

search.title: Search Projects
search.content: Search through your projects by name

summary.title: Project Summary
summary.content: View a summary of all your projects

sort.title: Sort Projects
sort.content: Sort your projects by name, last opened date, or last modified date

project_list.title: Project list
project_list.content: Here you can find all your projects. Click on any project to open it. By clicking … in the bottom right corner, you can access a menu to rename, edit the description, or delete the project.

rules_table.title: Rules table
rules_table.content: A list of generated rules with their conclusions (decisions based on the rule), precision, and coverage. The “Column selector” button allows you to display additional indicators.

recent_project_list.title: Example projects
recent_project_list.content: Here you will find example projects with preloaded datasets and generated rule sets for different problem types. Clicking on a project will open it and add it to your project list. You can work freely on example projects and upload new ones at any time.

treeView.title: Tree View
treeView.content: This element represents a dataset. Left-clicking will display it in the main part of the application. Right-clicking or selecting the three dots on the right opens a context menu with additional options, such as generating a rule set.

rulesets_group.title: Rule sets
rulesets_group.content: This element groups rule sets associated with the dataset it belongs to. Right-clicking or selecting the three dots on the right opens a context menu where you can generate a new rule set or compare existing ones.

ruleSetItem.title: Rule set
ruleSetItem.content: This element represents a rule set (generated, created, added, or imported) for the associated dataset. Left-clicking will display it in the main part of the application. Right-clicking or selecting the three dots opens a context menu allowing you to perform operations such as filtering to reduce the number of rules.

tabBar.title: Tab Bar
tabBar.content: Switch between different project views using the tab bar.

subTabButton.title: Sub Tab Button
subTabButton.content: Navigate to specific sections using sub-tab buttons.

dataset_view_table.title: Dataset view table
dataset_view_table.content: In this table you can explore the dataset. Options include filtering and sorting examples. You can sort by multiple columns by holding the “Shift” key. The column selector allows you to hide specific columns. You can also export the dataset to a .csv or .xlsx file. Clicking the floppy disk icon saves the dataset as a new one (overwriting is not possible). Saving takes into account filtering, sorting, and hidden columns.

description.title: Dataset description
description.content: In this section you can edit and view the dataset description. Add context, source information, and a brief overview of attributes.

dataset_information.title: Dataset information
dataset_information.content: This section provides detailed information about the dataset, along with suggestions for columns that can be modified to achieve more precise results.

numerical_attributes.title: Numerical attributes
numerical_attributes.content: The table displays the dataset’s numerical attributes along with their statistics.

nominal_attributes.title: Nominal attributes
nominal_attributes.content: For each attribute, you can see the number of missing values and the most frequent value, which helps identify dominant categories.

dataset_correlation_matrix.title: Data correlation matrix
dataset_correlation_matrix.content: The visualization shows the correlation matrix for numerical attributes.

dataset_histogram_chart.title: Numerical attribute chart
dataset_histogram_chart.content: A chart displaying histograms for numerical attributes. You can adjust the number of bins and select the attribute to analyze. The default number of bins is determined automatically based on the data.

histogram_chart.title: Histogram Chart
histogram_chart.content: This chart displays the distribution of values for a selected attribute.

rolap_dataset_bar_chart.title: Nominal attribute chart
rolap_dataset_bar_chart.content: This panel allows you to analyze the distribution of values for a selected nominal attribute.

rules_prediction_indicators.title: Prediction metrics
rules_prediction_indicators.content: A summary of prediction quality metrics obtained by the rule set on the dataset it is linked to (most often the training set).

rules_quantitative_characteristics.title: Quantitative characteristics of the rule set
rules_quantitative_characteristics.content: A summary of the statistics of the rule set determined on the dataset it is linked to.

rules_importance_card.title: Importance of conditions and attributes (by class)
rules_importance_card.content: A comparison showing which conditions and attributes are most important in a given class, i.e. those with the greatest impact on the decision.

project_rules_coverage.title: Rule coverage in the project
project_rules_coverage.content: A view of rules with the “Filter dataset” and “Show coverage” columns. Selecting “Filter dataset” filters the dataset according to the rule, so only matching examples are shown in the table below. You can select multiple rules and choose whether to show all examples covered by any of them (OR) or only those matching all rules (AND). The “Show coverage” option highlights the examples covered by a rule, helping to assess its usefulness.

project_rules_coverage_table.title: Rule coverage table
project_rules_coverage_table.content: A table of examples covered by rules, showing the number of rules covering each row, the predicted class, and the actual label.

comparison_form.title: Rule comparison form
comparison_form.content: Configuration of rule comparison settings. The options determine how the comparison is performed.

comparison_rules_table.title: Rule comparison table
comparison_rules_table.content: A table that allows you to select rules for comparison and analyze their structure.

alignment_button_group.title: Analysis modes
alignment_button_group.content: A toggle between the “Rule set” and “Importance” modes. It allows quick switching of the analysis perspective.

rules_and_conditions_select_list.title: Rule and condition selection list
rules_and_conditions_select_list.content: A selection list of rules and their conditions to be visualized.

visualisation_coverage_info.title: Information on graph-selected conditions
visualisation_coverage_info.content: After selecting a condition (or multiple) on the graph, information about their combination is displayed. For classification, this is the number of examples from a given class covered by the condition(s). For regression, it is a histogram of decision attribute values. For survival analysis, it is a survival curve based on the covered examples.

rolap_graph_plot.title: Rule set graph
rolap_graph_plot.content: A graph-based visualization. The edges from conditions display information about them. In classification, this is the number of examples from a given class covered by the condition. In regression, it is the mean and standard deviation of the decision attribute. In survival analysis, it is the time when the probability of the event drops below 50% for the covered examples.

prediction_settings.title: Prediction settings
prediction_settings.content: Configuration of prediction settings. Works similarly to the Predictions tab.

prediction_result.title: Prediction
prediction_result.content: A table of prediction results for the selected dataset. Right-clicking a row allows you to go to the “Explain example” tab to see the basis for the model’s decision.

prediction_computer.title: Prediction for external dataset
prediction_computer.content: You can run a prediction on your own file. Set the encoding (e.g., UTF-8), field separator, and decimal separator, then drag and drop the file to start the process. The result will be a file with an additional column containing the model’s predictions.

prediction_test_left.title: Prediction quality – training set
prediction_test_left.content: A table with model quality metrics calculated on the training data.

prediction_test_right.title: Prediction quality – test set
prediction_test_right.content: A table with model quality metrics calculated on the test data.

project_example.title: Decision explanation
project_example.content: This tab allows you to check why the model made a specific decision for a given example. You can select an example from the dataset, pick one randomly, or enter it manually. After selection, you can analyze the decision and the rules that led to it.

description_left.title: Rule set name and description
description_left.content: A form for editing the name and description of the rule set.

description_right.title: Rule set creation details
description_right.content: A table containing the algorithm parameters and prediction settings used to generate the rule set.

algorithm.title: Algorithm selection
algorithm.content: Choose how to build the rule set: using the RuleKit algorithm, DeepRules algorithm, or manually. The choice determines the available configuration options.

algorithm_configuration.title: Algorithm configuration
algorithm_configuration.content: In the simple configuration, you answer questions and the system automatically selects algorithm parameters. In the advanced configuration, you can manually adjust all parameters.

generate-button.title: Rule set generation
generate-button.content: Final step – click “Create” to start generating. Progress will be visible in the “Processes” interface, and once completed, you will be redirected to the analysis view of the new rule set.
